messages.content: Help me create a VMDeathRequest with a suspend policy of EVENT_THREAD and a property 'testProperty' set to 'deathEvent001' in a Java debugging session?

function.name: suspendpolicy017_settingVMDeathRequest
function.description: Creates a VMDeathRequest with the specified suspend policy and property. Throws a JDITestRuntimeException if the request cannot be set. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

suspendPolicy.description: The suspend policy to be used for the VMDeathRequest. This is Java integer type parameter in string representation.

property.description: The property to be associated with the VMDeathRequest. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to create a VMDeathRequest with a suspend policy of EVENT_THREAD and a property 'testProperty' set to 'deathEvent001' in a Java debugging session. We have a tool function named suspendpolicy017_settingVMDeathRequest that takes suspendPolicy (string) and property (string). We need to call this function with appropriate arguments.

We need to provide the suspend policy as a string. The suspend policy "EVENT_THREAD" likely corresponds to a constant in the Java Debug Interface (JDI). In JDI, suspend policies are defined as constants: EventRequest.SUSPEND_NONE, SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD, SUSPEND_ALL. So we want to use "SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD". But the user says "EVENT_THREAD". Possibly they refer to the constant name "EVENT_THREAD" which might be part of the JDI's EventRequest.SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD. So we should pass "SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD" or maybe just "EVENT_THREAD"? The function expects a string representation of the Java integer type parameter. That means we need to pass the integer value of the suspend policy. In JDI, SUSPEND_NONE=0, SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD=1, SUSPEND_ALL=2. So we need to pass "1" as the suspendPolicy argument. The property is a string "testProperty" set to "deathEvent001". The function signature only has two parameters: suspendPolicy and property. It doesn't accept a property name; it just accepts a property string. So we can pass "deathEvent001" as the property. The property name is not passed. So we call the function with suspendPolicy="1" and property="deathEvent001".

Thus we will call the function:

{
  "suspendPolicy": "1",
  "property": "deathEvent001"
}
